lesson_title: The Notebook for Money Coming In
hook_text: One quick sum tells you whether a month of money records is right. Here it is.
clip_script: Every rand a shop receives goes into one notebook: the cash receipts journal. Each line: the proof, the day, who paid, and the amount in the bank column. Then one more column says what kind of money it was. Cash sales go in sales, with a note of what the goods cost. Everything else, capital, rent, a loan, interest, goes in sundry, which just means other. At the end of March, Ridgeview Hardware adds up its columns. Bank: R140 250. Sales: R27 600. Sundry: R112 650. Now the check. Every rand in the bank column must also sit in sales or sundry. So sales plus sundry must equal bank. 27 600 plus 112 650: R140 250. It matches. The cost of sales note stays out of the check, because no money came in for it. If the sum does not match, a rand is hiding somewhere, and now you know how to find it.
visual_style: A ruled journal page filling in line by line with column headings lit up, then column totals sliding into an addition that clicks against the bank total with a green tick.
pacing: Line-by-line rhythm, a pause before the cross-cast, a crisp finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and complete Ridgeview Hardware's CRJ yourself.
